unit.sep: Collect,organise,represent,interpret and communicate data with a stated frame and uncertainty.
unit.careers: Illustrative data-recording,analysis and school-planning practices;no professional statistical or safety certification.
unit.focus: Actual safe classroom data,grouped/ungrouped tables and summaries,equal/unequal density histograms,frequency polygons and bounded decisions.
unit.phenomenon: A fictional box-inventory report treats missing records as good condition and uses the tallest unequal-width bar as the largest count.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Actual classroom records,separate fictional data,weighted averages,midpoint/interpolation assumptions,density areas and checked digital graphs.
unit.drivingQuestion: Which data and representations justify a local decision? KICD: What is statistics?; How do we represent data?; How do we use statistics in day-to-day life?
unit.storylineThread: Plan → collect → ungrouped table → grouped table → mean → median/mode → grouped mean → grouped median → grouped mode → equal histogram → unequal histogram → polygon → actual digital analysis → communicate → audit → independent evidence.
unit.content: Collection of Data; Frequency distribution table; Mean, Mode and Median of grouped and ungrouped data; Representation of Data; Interpretation of Data
unit.coreCompetencies:
Critical thinking and problem solving: the learner uses the histograms and frequency polygons to examine data and make conclusions.
Self-Efficacy: the learner discusses with peers the meaning of the term data and explores data sources.
Digital literacy: the learner uses digital devices to draw histograms and frequency polygons to make conclusions.
Communication and collaboration: learner presents and shares findings from data to different groups of people such as school administrators, parents or local community leaders.
unit.values:
Integrity: the learner collects and records data accurately.
Unity: the learner works in groups and uses collected data to draw histograms and frequency polygons.
Love: the learner is considerate of the other as they discuss in pairs and identify the modal class for grouped data
unit.pcis:
Life Skills (Decision Making): the learner makes informed decisions from data interpretation from histograms and frequency polygons.
Parental Engagement and Empowerment: the learner seeks support and guidance from parents or guardians to collect, organise and present data on an identified situation in the school or community.

assessment.instructions: Lesson16,40minutes:4procedure,16sections1–2,12section3,4section4,4checking/collection. Work independently with SI16 only,calculator,ruler and pencil. Use the two blank panels for separate graphs and label linear scales/units. No teaching cards,software,peers or hints. Fictional data do not certify actual collection or digital action.

sections.title: 1. Ungrouped organisation and summaries
sections.prompt: For SI16 FinalA,draw a value/frequency table and check its total. Determine mean,median and mode with evidence. Explain why an average need not be one of the observations.
sections.exemplar: Values2,3,5,7,10withfrequencies1,2,1,1,1,total6,sum30. Mean5,median(3+5)/2=4,mode3. Mean/median may be calculated values absent from the list;keep distinct definitions.

sections.title: 2. Grouped estimates
sections.prompt: For FinalB,add midpoint,fx and cumulative-frequency columns. Determine estimated mean,median and mode;identify median/modal classes. Use median≈L+((N/2-cfbefore)/f)h and equal-width mode≈L+[(fm-fprev)/(2fm-fprev-fnext)]h. State why these are estimates rather than recovered raw observations. Round calculated estimates to2decimalplaces where needed.
sections.exemplar: Midpoints15,25,35;fx45,125,140;sum310,N12;cum3,8,12. Meanestimate25.83cm,medianclass20–30 andmedianestimate26cm;modalclass20–30 andmodeestimate26.67cm. Midpoint/within-class interpolation assumptions;raw observations and exact repeated values unavailable.

sections.title: 3. Represent and interpret classes
sections.prompt: For FinalB,draw a density histogram on panel1 and a midpoint-frequency polygon on panel2;label variables,units,scales and title. State one valid count comparison. For FinalC,calculate each class width/density;identify the highest-density class and explain whether it also has uniquely highest frequency.

sections.title: 4. Make a bounded decision and identify missing evidence
sections.prompt: Suggest one modest use of the supplied distribution and one limitation on its interpretation. Propose a feasible real classroom collection/follow-up plan that would improve a local decision. Name one separate actual observation needed to certify your collection or digital graphing skill. Explain why the fictional record cannot establish a whole-school causal claim.
sections.exemplar: Accept a proportional size/storage planning check tied to the supplied length distribution,with limited frame/fictional status/grouping uncertainty. Plan specifies safe accessible source,variable/unit,recording and missing/duplicate check. Actual individual measurement/recording or digital graph/save action must be observed separately;writing a plan is not performing it. No causal/whole-school generalisation from these fictional grouped data.
